name: PRDBench
intro: PRDBench 是面向真实 PRD 的项目级代码智能体基准。论文 v3 报告 50 个 Python 项目、20 个领域和 1,258 个评分点（408 个单元测试、732 个 Shell 交互、118 个文件比较）；固定官方 Git/HF 快照实际包含 1,259 个评分点，其中多 1 个文件比较项。
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Meituan, AGI-Eval
build_method: 智能体初始化PRD与AAA指标, 生成脚手架和评测标准, 人工检查, 至少五轮人机修订, 移除脚手架
task_type: 项目级代码生成, 软件工程, 调试
eval_feature: PRD驱动, 三类可执行标准, 专用PRDJudge, 0/1/2逐项评分, 开发与调试双轮
scale: 论文v3：50个任务、20个领域、1,258项；固定Git/HF：1,259项
task_type_en: Project-level code generation, software engineering, debugging
build_method_en: Agent-initialized PRDs and AAA outlines, scaffold and criteria generation, human inspection, at least five human-agent refinement rounds, scaffold removal
eval_feature_en: PRD-driven, three executable criterion types, dedicated PRDJudge, per-item 0/1/2 scoring, development and debugging rounds
intro_en: PRDBench evaluates project-level code agents from real PRDs. Paper v3 reports 50 Python projects across 20 domains and 1,258 scoring points (408 unit tests, 732 shell interactions, and 118 file comparisons); the pinned official Git/HF snapshot contains 1,259 points, with one additional file-comparison item.
scale_en: Paper v3: 50 tasks, 20 domains, 1,258 points; pinned Git/HF: 1,259 points

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; source_scope=paper-v3 plus immutable official Git and Hugging Face snapshots. PAPER: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24358v3 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.24358v3. arXiv identifies v3 as the 2026-03-23 revision accepted by AAMAS 2026. The downloaded v3 PDF has SHA-256 c9b6ac8d4e97c1b821ac5dd5cbb600be59d271614094899ec330e32046b55469. CODE: https://github.com/AGI-Eval-Official/PRDBench/tree/050bbcbd1332d94f031d67ca4427af0e48c58c91. The pinned repository root tree is 7902a5a3af2009ed86cef66ce6ba2937341190a4 and its PRDBench data subtree is 77f22c9b24ad6a1b1d46da13b180592df9c9bfc2. DATA MIRROR: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AGI-Eval/PRDbench/tree/9eaa70817b224e404c21b56bc732c997cb40c3db; its repository tree is dedf1c5dcc09a44c8e29e02cab118dbd0c618070, data subtree is 4994faf27324661cc1733905c2c4e1bc34b9f7c8, and README LFS payload SHA-256 is 4b7eefef924d1254eed2b98ad07fcc4357e7b0e4f083b279ec38cac5adce82f5. CONSTRUCTION: paper section 3 and Figure 1 define five stages. Seed tasks come from internal AI-product development requests, public CS-course final projects on GitHub, and code-reproduction tasks derived from CS theses. A seed must be fully implementable in Python and all associated datasets must be publicly accessible. GPT-4 assigns domain labels before strategic sampling; rare domains retain at least one representative, while common domains are sampled for diverse techniques and subskills, yielding 50 projects across 20 domains. Step 1 uses code agents such as Claude Code to write standardized PRDs with requirement overview, functional requirements, and data requirements. GPT-4.1 converts each PRD into an Arrange-Act-Assert metric outline: Arrange prepares files, data, and environment; Act runs the program or interaction; Assert compares system response or state to the expected result. Step 2 uses a SOTA code agent to create a module/interface scaffold, then expands the outline into a detailed criteria scheme with executable commands, interfaces, artifacts, inputs, and expected outputs. The paper explicitly permits an algorithm inside the temporary scaffold to remain imperfect when that does not obstruct annotation; the scaffold is an annotation aid, not a released reference solution. Step 3 limits human work to executing tests and checking that interfaces work and expected outputs agree with the PRD. Step 4 sends identified defects as targeted feedback to the code agent, which revises the scaffold or criteria, followed by reinspection. The strict inclusion rule is at least five human-agent refinement rounds and resolution of all observed issues. Step 5 removes the generated scaffold and retains only PRD, criteria scheme, test artifacts, and data, forcing evaluated agents to implement from scratch. COUNT RECONCILIATION: paper v3 section 3.3 states 1,258 metrics: 408 Unit Test, 732 Shell Interaction, and 118 File Comparison. This arithmetic is internally consistent. A direct parse of all 50 detailed_test_plan.json files at Git commit 050bbcbd1332d94f031d67ca4427af0e48c58c91 instead yields 1,259 records: 408 unit_test, 732 shell_interaction, and 119 file_comparison. The fixed HF mirror exposes the same 50-task layout. The diagram therefore preserves the paper-defined 1,258 count on the main construction path and places the 1,259 public-snapshot count in a dashed release boundary. The former 1,262 / 409 / 729 / 124 page values were removed because they match neither the v3 paper nor the pinned release. EVALUATION: Round 1 DEVELOPMENT supplies PRD.md and evaluation/detailed_test_plan.json and asks the code agent to implement the complete project under src. PRDJudge evaluates every criterion with the submitted code, test assets, commands, inputs, and expected outputs. Paper section 4.1 discloses six tool categories spanning file read/write, system command execution, image handling through deal_graph, and a specialized interactive judge tool; the paper uses GPT-4o behind deal_graph for multimodal outputs. Unit tests run the provided pytest-style command, shell-interaction criteria replay simulated user inputs and inspect logs, and file-comparison criteria execute generation commands before comparing produced artifacts with references. The official score_cal.py at the fixed commit sums 0/1/2 criterion scores, divides by the number of valid criterion records and by two, then averages available project scores. Round 2 DEBUG gives the code agent the first-round deduction report, asks it to repair failed criteria, and reruns the same evaluator. This is a two-round evaluation loop, not a second benchmark-construction pass. PRDJUDGE TRAINING: paper section 4.2 starts with Qwen3-Coder-480B-A3B as an initial judge and collects trajectories over outputs from 11 code agents, randomly sampling eight repositories per agent. Two humans independently label each scoring point with 2=pass, 1=partial, or 0=fail; a senior annotator arbitrates disagreements. From 2,147 candidate trajectories, exact final-score agreement with human labels retains 1,742; a second rule-based filter removes excessive length and invalid tool use, yielding 911 training trajectories. PRDJudge fine-tunes Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B using LoRA rank 16 for one epoch, learning rate 2e-4, warmup ratio 0.03, on eight H800 GPUs. The paper reports in-domain HAR 91.75 and out-of-domain HAR 92.69, but these validation results are not additional construction steps. MODEL BOUNDARY: the paper specifies the base model and complete training recipe, while neither the pinned Git tree nor the pinned HF dataset publishes an immutable PRDJudge checkpoint. The public Evaluation code therefore still requires users to configure a model endpoint; the diagram marks the checkpoint as unavailable rather than inventing a model artifact. LICENSE BOUNDARY: the pinned Git repository has no root LICENSE file, although its README states that the project is MIT licensed. The pinned HF dataset card has no YAML license declaration. For that reason openness is recorded as mixed and the graph does not overstate a dataset-wide legal grant. LANGUAGE/TOPOLOGY REVIEW: the EN and ZH specs use identical semantic IDs, node types, sizes, positions, edges, waypoints, and dashed-secondary styles. English labels contain no Chinese text; Chinese labels carry equivalent semantics. The build path, judge-training branch, three test branches, DEBUG loop, fixed-count drift, missing checkpoint, and license ambiguity are all represented explicitly without converting boundary notes into workflow stages. Formal publication evidence [site-a12d-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3493×1545 (English) and 3493×1545 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3491×1543 and 3491×1543. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
